detail: Manufacturers and importers notify each product through HSA's PRISM system before supplying it. HSA acknowledges the notification but does not approve the product.

item: Check ingredients and labels against the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive
detail: Ingredients must follow the directive's annexes (prohibited, restricted and permitted lists) and the product must carry the required label information.
Keep it available for inspection, for at least 3 years after the product was last placed on the market.
Every product needs a Responsible Person established in the EU (Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009).

item: Complete a Cosmetic Product Safety Report
detail: A qualified safety assessor signs a safety report before the product is placed on the market.
Notify the product on the Cosmetic Products Notification Portal before it is placed on the market.
The label carries the INCI list, batch number, period after opening or date of minimum durability, and the Responsible Person's address.
Every product needs a Responsible Person based in the UK.
A UK safety report is signed by a qualified assessor before the product is placed on the market.
Notify the product through the UK Submit Cosmetic Product Notification service before it is placed on the market.
MoCRA requires registration of each facility that makes or processes cosmetics. Foreign facilities must name a US agent. Small businesses with average sales under USD 1 million may be exempt.
List each product with FDA through Cosmetics Direct, update the listing every year, and give the registration number of each facility.
The responsible person must hold adequate safety substantiation for the product.
Serious adverse events must be reported to FDA, and labels must carry the required contact details.
